chunks: Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. 'Amer narrated to us from his uncle 'Abdullah b. 'Amer, from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr. He said: A group of our shaykhs narrated to me, among them Aban b. 'Uthman, Hisham b. Salim, and Muhammad b. Humran, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
I am astonished at him who is alarmed by four things yet does not seek refuge in four [others].

I am astonished at him who fears the enemy, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Trustee.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So they returned with bounty from God and grace -- no harm touched them.'

And I am astonished at him who is anguished, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'There is no god except You; glory be to You, indeed I was from the wrongdoers.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So We answered him and rescued him from anguish -- and likewise, We rescue the believers.'

And I am astonished at him who is plotted against, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'And I delegate my affairs to God; indeed God watches over His servants.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'So God protected him from the evils of what they plotted.'

And I am astonished at him who desires this world and its adornments, yet does not seek refuge in His saying, the Exalted: 'Whatever God wills; there is no power except by God.' For indeed I have heard God, Mighty and Majestic, say following it: 'Although you see that I have less wealth and fewer children than you, then perhaps my Lord will grant me something better than your garden' -- and this 'perhaps' is an affirmation.

key_terms.بِعَقِبِهَا: following it / in its wake: Refers to the verse that immediately follows the supplication
key_terms.فَزِعَ: is alarmed/fears: Used in the sense of being gripped by anxiety or panic
key_terms.مُوجِبَةٌ: an affirmation / a certainty: The word عسى (perhaps) from God is an obligation, not a possibility
key_terms.يَفْزَعُ إِلَى: seeks refuge in: When followed by إلى, the verb shifts meaning from 'fears' to 'takes recourse to'

ai.seo_question: What are the four Quranic remedies for fear, grief, conspiracy, and worldly desire according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expresses astonishment at those who face four types of distress -- fear of the enemy, anguish, being plotted against, and desire for worldly things -- yet do not seek refuge in four corresponding Quranic verses. For each affliction, he identifies a specific supplication from the Quran and cites the divine promise that immediately follows it, demonstrating that God's response to sincere supplication is guaranteed. The Imam concludes by noting that the word 'perhaps' (asa) when used by God is an affirmation, not a mere possibility. This teaching was transmitted through multiple reliable narrators including Aban b. 'Uthman, Hisham b. Salim, and Muhammad b. Humran.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr. He said: A group of our shaykhs narrated to me, from whom were Aban b. `Uthman, Hisham b. Salim, and Muhammad b. Humran from Al-Sadiq (as). He said:
I am astonished at him who fears four things yet does not seek refuge in four [other] things.

(1) I am astonished at him who is afraid of the enemy: why does he not take his concern to His saying, “Allah is sufficient for us, for He is the best trustee” [3:173]? I have heard Allah follow it up with “So they returned by the bounty and the grace of Allah – no harm touched them.” [3:174]

(2) I am astonished at him who is anguished: why does he not take his concern to His saying: “There is no god except You, may You be glorified: surely, I was from the wrongdoers.” [21:87]? I have heard Allah follow it up with “We answered his prayer and rescued him from anguish – and like that, We rescue the believers.” [21:88]

(3) I am astonished at him who is plotted against: why does he not take his concern to His saying, “I delegate my affairs to Allah. Surely, Allah watches over His servants.” [40:44]? I have heard Allah follow it up with “Allah protected him from their evil plots” [40:45].

(4) I am astonished at him who wants this world and its frills: why does he not take his concern to His saying, “Whatever Allah wills; there is no power except by Allah.” [18:39]? I have heard Allah follow it up with “Although you see that I have less wealth and fewer sons than you, perhaps my Lord will grant me something better than your garden.” (18:38-39) – and this “perhaps” was delivered.
